chunks: 1541 - And in the narration of al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, he said:
“You say in the final sajdah of the salat of Ja‘far ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام:
O One who has clothed Himself with might and dignity, O One who has wrapped Himself in glory and has been ennobled by it, O One for whom glorification befits none but Him,
O One whose knowledge has encompassed and counted every thing,

O Possessor of blessing and abundance, O Possessor of favor and grace, O Possessor of power and generosity, I ask You by the bonds of might from Your Throne, and the utmost mercy from Your Book, and by Your greatest, highest Name, and Your perfect words, to send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and to do for me such and such.

key_terms.سَجْدَةٍ: prostration; here, the final sajdah in the prayer
key_terms.صَلَاةِ: salat (prayer); the devotional prayer being described
key_terms.عَرْشِكَ: Your Throne; a reference to divine sovereignty
key_terms.كَلِمَاتِكَ ٱلتَّامَّاتِ: Your perfect words; complete and flawless divine words
key_terms.مُحَمَّدٍ وَآلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: Muhammad and the family of Muhammad; the formula of salawat in the supplication
key_terms.ٱسْمِكَ ٱلْأَعْظَمِ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ: Your greatest and highest Name; an exalted divine invocation
key_terms.ٱلْعِزِّ: might and honor; divine majesty invoked in supplication

ai.seo_question: What supplication is recited in the final sajdah of the salat of Ja‘far ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a specific du'a to be recited in the final sajdah of the salat of Ja‘far ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام. It invokes Allah through His majesty, knowledge, mercy, and supreme Name, and concludes with salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and asking for one’s needs.
